finding: DSK entrepreneurship tables publish only the two latest years; the register only the latest period
consequence: archived DSK vintages recovered (Part 4): 006 for 2019, 2020, 2022-2024; register flows by section for 2021, 2024, 2025

finding: No archived vintage covers 2021 in entrepreneurship 006, nor full-year 2022-2023 register flows
evidence: Internet Archive holds 006 only for April 2022 and April 2025; 2_1 for Mar 2022, Aug 2022, Sep 2024, Apr 2025, Jul 2025, Feb 2026
consequence: the activity panel is unbalanced in time (2019, 2020, 2022, 2023, 2024); 2021 is not used in estimation; for charts and tables it is filled by interpolation and flagged (FR12_series_filled.csv, Part 7.1)

finding: Year 2023 is published in two vintages of 006; revisions recorded
consequence: the later vintage is used; NFR1 real-time caveat: hold-out actuals are the latest vintage

finding: Registered entrepreneurship subjects do not follow the stock-flow identity exactly
evidence: 2020: ΔN − (new − deregistered) = -17,137; 2023: ΔN − (new − deregistered) = +8,716; 2024: ΔN − (new − deregistered) = +6,653
consequence: registration-based rates use the end-year registered stock as denominator, as DSK does; reactivations / reclassifications are a residual

finding: Register stock by section does not follow N(t) = N(t-1) + new - liquidated exactly
evidence: 2025, sum over sections: +0 units; largest section gaps: S +129, L +50, G +36
consequence: section reclassifications in the register; the SYNTHETIC register reproduces births and deaths exactly and reports the stock gap (Part 17)

finding: Three different enterprise populations in the sources
evidence: registered entrepreneurship subjects (incl. individual entrepreneurs) 1,505,893 (2024) vs statistical units 226,643 (1 Jan 2026); active taxpayers 859,345 (2025)
consequence: each indicator states its population; rates are never mixed across populations
administrative registration of farmers (subsidy system) rather than market entry; agriculture kept in the panel, its fixed effect and a 2020 robustness check reported

finding: Workbook DVX: micro-taxpayer rows duplicate the budget-organisation rows
evidence: count, turnover and receipts identical in 4 years: yes
consequence: micro taxpayers excluded from the taxpayer size-class concentration; to be corrected by the Tax Service

finding: DSK 1_1_en.xls: section A row labelled 'of which:'
evidence: the agriculture row carries the label of the line above
consequence: FR12 parses size-class tables by section pattern and checks section sums against the published total

finding: Public administration (O) shows liquidations from administrative reorganisation
evidence: FY 2021: liquidated 71, new 20; FY 2024: liquidated 74, new 14; FY 2025: liquidated 167, new 37; H1 2022: liquidated 5, new 31; H1 2024: liquidated 38, new 10; H1 2025: liquidated 17, new 27; H1 2026: liquidated 228, new 10
consequence: O and U (extraterritorial) are non-market sections: excluded from competition indicators, kept in totals

finding: Workbook region sheets equal the DSK register by region
evidence: statistical units, new and liquidated: identical in 2021, 2024 and 2025 (asserted in Part 5)
consequence: the 2021-2025 region panel is a register series; regional entry/exit is modelled on it

finding: Size-class counts (1_3) cover commercial organisations only
evidence: large + medium + small + micro = 215,416 vs 232,847 statistical units (1 July 2026)
consequence: size-class concentration bounds use commercial-organisation counts

finding: January-June flows are not half of full-year flows
consequence: H1 files used only for descriptive monitoring; models use full-year flows

finding: Register liquidations are far below deregistrations of entrepreneurship subjects
evidence: register exit rate 0.31% (2025) vs deregistration rate 1.66% (2024, 006)
consequence: dormant legal units stay in the register: register exit understates market exit; exit forecasts use the 006 deregistration series

finding: SME output shares (012) and national-accounts output use different bases
evidence: in education and health the implied average SME revenue exceeds the statutory class ceiling when the share is applied to national-accounts output (public output in the base)
consequence: for those group-years the concentration upper bound drops the revenue caps (uncapped supremum) and is flagged
one-off administrative clean-up: a common 2022 impulse dummy in the exit equations, set to zero out of sample

finding: Definition change in DSK 006 between vintages
evidence: 2019-2020 vintage: 'newly created' / 'liquidated' enterprises (found: yes); 2022+ vintages: 'newly registered' / 'deregistered' (found: yes)
consequence: births equation carries a break term (1 from 2022); exit keeps the 2022 impulse only (2023-2024 exit levels close to 2019-2020: no persistent break evident)

finding: Inspection counts change coverage over time
evidence: total inspections 17 (2015), 1,648 (2019), 17,082 (2020), 50,071 (2025); the Ministry of Emergency Situations' fire-safety inspections enter from 2020 and utility inspections (Azərişıq, Azəriqaz) from 2021-2022
consequence: inspections are not comparable across years and are not used in the early-warning composite; reported as information only
